title: Set up a 401(k)
summary: Stand up the retirement plan (now state-mandated in California and a dozen others): pick a provider, decide the match, sign the plan adoption agreement, connect payroll, and verify the first contribution syncs.

parts.title: Pick a 401(k) provider
parts.guidance: Compare providers against workforce needs, proposed plan design, payroll integration and the team’s administrative capacity. Examine fees, investments, support, data handling and the exact service responsibilities, including duties retained by the employer. Bring the tradeoffs to the plan sponsor before engagement. Identify the payroll, finance and people contacts who will operate the selected arrangement.

parts.title: Decide employer match and eligibility
parts.guidance: Model contribution designs against the workforce and budget with the plan adviser. Resolve eligibility, entry dates, compensation definitions, vesting and any automatic-enrollment features under current requirements. Take the cost and design choices to the company’s decision makers before configuration or announcement. Compare the adoption documents with the settled terms, paying attention to selections that differ from provider defaults.

parts.title: Sign the plan adoption agreement
parts.guidance: Compare the adoption agreement and underlying plan documents with the chosen contribution formulas, eligibility, effective dates and administrative responsibilities. Resolve discrepancies with the adviser before the authorized sponsor signatory executes. Give payroll and the administrator the implementation details drawn from the signed plan, including the provisions that differ from standard provider settings.

parts.title: Connect the payroll integration
parts.guidance: Map employee identifiers, eligible compensation, deferrals, employer contributions and any loan repayments between payroll and the plan system. Check integration permissions with the account owners before connecting. Verify the mapping through the provider’s supported test or preview process, paying attention to rejected records and corrections. Agree who reconciles each payroll run to contributions received and allocated by the plan.

parts.title: Announce enrollment to the team
parts.guidance: Explain enrollment using the adopted plan’s participant materials: who can act, where to enroll, what choices are available and where questions go. Check the required notices and audience with the plan administrator before sending. Help employees resolve access problems while leaving contribution and investment elections to them. Make the official plan information easy to find beyond the initial announcement.

parts.title: Verify the first contribution sync
parts.guidance: Match the first payroll’s deductions and employer contributions to amounts received by the plan and allocated to participant accounts, using the responsible provider’s records. Reconcile participants, pay periods, contribution types and totals, and investigate missing or rejected records promptly. Have the plan owner check deposit timing against applicable requirements and the actual payroll date. Resolve discrepancies beyond any integration success message.

metadata.supportReason: Modern 401(k) providers onboard online and sync payroll automatically; the match decision and the plan adoption signature stay with the founder.

geoNotes.summary: The EPF is the mandatory retirement vehicle once headcount crosses 20 — 12% of basic pay from employer and employee each, administered through the EPFO employer portal.
Not optional like a 401(k): every UK employer must auto-enrol eligible staff into a workplace pension (8% minimum combined contribution) and declare compliance to The Pensions Regulator.

State pension contributions ride payroll automatically; the 401(k) analog is betriebliche Altersvorsorge — every employer MUST offer salary conversion (Entgeltumwandlung) with a 15% employer top-up when social charges are saved.

Mandatory complementary pensions (AGIRC-ARRCO) enroll automatically through payroll's DSN — nothing to set up; the optional analog is a PER d'entreprise (collective retirement savings plan) as a perk.

State pension contributions ride the single social-security charge automatically and no occupational plan is mandated — a company PPR (retirement-savings plan) is a voluntary perk rather than an expected setup project.

CPP rides payroll automatically; the 401(k) analog is the voluntary group RRSP or DPSP most tech employers offer (Quebec alone mandates offering a plan, the VRSP, for established employers with staff there).
